startHere.text: Compiled from the training system and drills discussed in this conversation. Includes nine-zone work, progression drills, live-BP constraints, and blank tracking tools.

The original document contained numbered citations without a source list. This workbook does not treat those references as verified sources. Coaching cues and numerical advancement targets are planning suggestions, not validated universal standards.
Inside/outside are relative to the hitter. Pull and opposite-field lanes reverse for left-handed and right-handed hitters. Zone numbering remains unchanged.
Contact-depth descriptions reproduce the supplied coaching framework. Treat foot/toe/back-hip references as individualized starting cues rather than fixed measurements.
Select two priority zones and one cue. Begin at the level where the hitter can perform the assignment. Add one demand at a time; review results between rounds.

Use appropriate protective equipment, screens, supervision, and age-appropriate speeds. Live pitchers should follow applicable workload and rest limits; this workbook is not a pitcher workload prescription. Do not shorten live-pitch distance to increase challenge.

Record actual pitch location. Mark an unintended delivery as off-plan; exclude it from assignment-specific measures when the assignment cannot reasonably be executed. Evaluate swing/take decisions using actual ball/strike location.
Use N/A when a denominator is zero. Recognition requires an explicit recorded ball/strike call. A taken strike is a decision error only when the round assignment calls for swinging at that strike.
Enter one pitch per row in Pitch Log. Dashboard formulas use rows 2–501 and assume one session per copy of the workbook. Rates on Daily Log are entered manually from the session dashboard.

9 zone-covering strikes + 6 weak-zone strikes + 3 obvious balls

Do not force all baseline volume into one session

codingGuide.rule: 1 if swing/take matched actual pitch and predeclared assignment; 0 otherwise. Leave blank for forced takes or nondecision rounds.
1 only when pitch was an actual strike and hitter swung. Record 0 otherwise.
1 only for swing at actual ball. Selective assignment errors on strikes are not chases.
1 for fair ball in play from swing at strike; 0 for foul, miss, or no swing.
1 for any bat contact on strike swing, including foul.
1 for agreed hard contact in assigned lane on strike swing; 0 for other eligible strike swings; blank if ineligible.
1/0 on strike swings only; blank on balls and takes. Use agreed individualized reference.
1/0 for balls in play on strikes only; blank otherwise.
1 for swing with one or more observed posture errors; 0 for stable swing; blank for takes. This counts affected swings, not individual faults.
Only enter if explicit ball/strike call was recorded. Use 1 correct, 0 incorrect.
1 if delivery missed planned training condition; do not automatically label hitter outcome a failure.
Keep counts alongside rates. Zero balls means chase rate N/A, not 0%. Do not rank zones from a handful of pitches.
